case: 15 Post-Election Trials: A Window into Courts in Belarus
outcome_summary: The report records 14 convictions among 15 defendants; the remaining defendant was released pending further investigation.
notes: 14 convicted; one unresolved. Aggregate classification rule needed.

case: Belarus v. Katsiaryna Andreyeva and Daria Chultsova
outcome_summary: Both journalists were convicted on 18 February 2021 and sentenced to two years in the monitored public-order case; their later releases do not establish reversal of that verdict.
notes: 2026 pardon not shown to cover the monitored 2021 conviction.

outcome_summary: Kak Sovannchhay was released in November 2021 after the remainder of his eight-month sentence was suspended; his conviction was upheld in December 2022.
notes: Suspended remainder, not acquittal; judicial supervision remained.

outcome_summary: Kong Raiya was convicted on 19 June 2020 and given a two-year suspended sentence with credit for time served.
notes: Pretrial release and a suspended sentence did not overturn the conviction.

outcome_summary: The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Ros Sokhet's detention arbitrary in November 2021; he later completed his sentence and was released.
notes: UN finding, not acquittal; release followed completion of sentence.

outcome_summary: The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Theary Seng's detention arbitrary in June 2023 and called for her release.
notes: UN finding; the cited source says she remains imprisoned.

case: Cambodia vs. Uon Chhin and Yeang Sothearin
outcome_summary: The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Uon Chhin and Yeang Sothearin's detention arbitrary in 2019.
notes: UN finding applies to both; it is not an acquittal or dismissal.

case: El Salvador: The Case Against Diana
outcome_summary: The court dismissed the charges against Diana for lack of evidence.
notes: Dismissal, not a conviction; Diana is a pseudonym.

case: Final Report: The Case of Paul Rusesabagina
outcome_summary: Paul Rusesabagina's 25-year prison sentence was commuted in 2023, and he was released and reunited with his family.
notes: Commutation and release; no acquittal recorded.

case: Government of Thailand & Chaiwat Limlikhitaksorn v. Wuth Boonlert & Samak Donnapee
outcome_summary: Wuth Boonlert and Samak Donnapee were both acquitted in the monitored defamation proceedings.
notes: Acquittals apply to both named defendants.

case: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region v. Bao Choy Yuk-ling
outcome_summary: Hong Kong's Court of Final Appeal overturned Bao Choy Yuk-ling's convictions on both counts on 5 June 2023.
notes: 2023 reversal supersedes the original 2021 conviction.

case: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region v. Tam Tak-chi
outcome_summary: Tam Tak-chi's 2022 convictions and 40-month prison sentence remained in place after his final appeal was dismissed on 6 March 2025.
notes: Final appeal rejected; no current custody status inferred.

case: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region v. Tong Ying-kit
outcome_summary: Tong Ying-kit was convicted of inciting secession and terrorist activities and sentenced to nine years in prison in 2021.
notes: Historical conviction; later reversal not confirmed in this review.

outcome_summary: Suzethe Margaret was found not guilty because of her psychosocial disability; the detention order was immediately suspended.
notes: Suspended detention order does not establish a conviction.

outcome_summary: Aigul Utepova was convicted in April 2021, sentenced to one year of restricted liberty and community service, and barred from civic activity for two years.
notes: Appeal rejected; a call to overturn is not an actual reversal.

outcome_summary: The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Alnur Ilyashev's detention arbitrary in March 2022 and called for his conviction to be quashed.
notes: UN finding; quashing was requested, not confirmed.

case: Kazakhstan v. Askhat Zheksebaev et al.
outcome_summary: Askhat Zheksebaev's five-year prison sentence was suspended in April 2022, and he was released in May 2022 with restrictions on activism and movement.
notes: Applies to Zheksebaev only; co-defendants' outcomes are not classified.

case: Malaysia v. Malaysiakini and Steven Gan
outcome_summary: Malaysiakini was convicted of contempt of court, while its editor Steven Gan was acquitted.
notes: Company convicted; editor acquitted. Aggregate classification rule needed.

outcome_summary: OMCT reported on 13 May 2026 that Kenia Hernandez remained imprisoned despite closure of eight federal cases, with two state cases and related appeals remaining.
notes: Still imprisoned as of May 2026; closed cases did not secure release.

outcome_summary: Omar Radi was convicted of insulting the judiciary on 17 March 2020 and received a four-month suspended sentence and a 500-dirham fine.
notes: 2020 tweet case; do not transfer the later case's pardon to this verdict.

outcome_summary: Omar Radi was pardoned and released on 29 July 2024 after serving part of his six-year sentence in the espionage and rape case.
notes: 2021 case; pardon and release do not mean acquittal.

case: Nigeria v. Eromosele Adene and Nicholas Mbah
outcome_summary: Adene's charges were dismissed in October 2021, while Mbah's proceedings were still ongoing when CFJ reported on the cases.
notes: Adene dismissed; Mbah unresolved. Aggregate classification rule needed.

case: Poland vs. Elzbieta Podlesna, Anna Prus, and Joanna Gzyra-Iskandar
defendants: Elzbieta Podlesna; Anna Prus; Joanna Gzyra-Iskandar
outcome_summary: All three women were acquitted in the Rainbow Virgin Mary case, and the prosecution's appeal was dismissed on 12 January 2022.
notes: January 2022 appeal result independently corroborated by Amnesty.

outcome_summary: Aleksey Navalny was convicted and fined in the monitored 2021 criminal slander case concerning comments about a war veteran.
notes: This row concerns the slander case, not his separate prison sentences.

outcome_summary: Mikhail Benyash was convicted again and fined on 6 March 2023 following a retrial after his earlier conviction was overturned.
notes: The earlier reversal was followed by a new conviction.

outcome_summary: Anastasia Shevchenko's monitored-case conviction remained in place; after conversion of her suspended sentence to imprisonment in December 2022, the term was reduced by one year in February 2023.
notes: Later sentence changed; reduction did not overturn the conviction.

outcome_summary: Svetlana Prokopyeva's conviction for justifying terrorism and 500,000-ruble fine were upheld by the military appeal court on 2 February 2021.
notes: Appeal upheld conviction; an unrelated civil dismissal is not acquittal.

case: Socialist Republic of Vietnam v. Pham Thi Doan Trang
outcome_summary: The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Pham Thi Doan Trang's detention arbitrary on 25 October 2021 and called for her release.
notes: UN finding; her later nine-year conviction was upheld on appeal.

case: Thailand v. Does 1-5 of the Organization for Thai Federation
outcome_summary: Four defendants were convicted of secret-society membership and acquitted of sedition in January 2020; the fifth defendant had fled before trial.
notes: Four convicted of one charge; fifth unresolved. Group rule needed.

case: The Trial of the Peacock Generation Troupe: Myanmar
outcome_summary: Six of seven troupe members were convicted in the monitored trial; three later received an amnesty and three others had already been released.
notes: Different verdicts and release routes. Aggregate classification rule needed.

case: Trial Monitoring of People v. Cansu Pişkin
outcome_summary: Cansu Piskin was found guilty on 7 May 2019 and given a ten-month prison sentence, which the court deferred.
notes: Deferred sentence; later dismissal or reversal unconfirmed.

case: Trial Monitoring of Proceedings against Ahmed Manseri
outcome_summary: Ahmed Manseri was acquitted in the monitored prosecution over his allegation of police torture.
notes: Acquittal in this case; later, separate charges are not included.

outcome_summary: Emna Chargui was convicted in July 2020 and sentenced to six months in prison and a 2,000-dinar fine for reposting a satirical text.
notes: Later appeal result unconfirmed; advocacy for reversal is not acquittal.

outcome_summary: Veysel Ok was convicted on 12 September 2019 and received a five-month suspended prison sentence.
notes: Suspension does not establish acquittal; later dismissal unconfirmed.

outcome_summary: Ahmet Tuna Altinel was acquitted of terrorist-propaganda charges in the monitored case, and the regional appeal court affirmed the acquittal.
notes: Monitored case only; passport restrictions are a separate issue.

outcome_summary: The court dismissed the unlawful-assembly charges against Moses Bwayo because the prosecution presented no witnesses.
notes: Dismissal confirmed; the machine's unknown suggestion was incomplete.

outcome_summary: Uganda's High Court overturned Stella Nyanzi's conviction and sentence on 20 February 2020, and she was released the same day.
notes: Reversal confirmed; release was not merely bail.

outcome_summary: Vannesa Rosales pleaded guilty to one abortion-related charge on 21 July 2021 and was sentenced to community service.
notes: Guilty plea and community service, not acquittal or complete dismissal.

outcome_summary: Alexander Pichugin was convicted in the monitored fake-news prosecution and fined 300,000 rubles.
notes: Historical conviction; later reversal not confirmed in this review.

outcome_summary: Mir Shakeel-ur-Rehman was acquitted in the monitored land-allotment corruption case on 31 January 2022 for lack of evidence.
notes: 2022 acquittal; his November 2020 bail was not the final outcome.

outcome_summary: Nariman Dzhelyal was released on 28 June 2024 in a prisoner exchange before completing his 17-year sentence.
notes: Prisoner exchange, not pardon or acquittal; applies to Dzhelyal.

case: Fairness Report: Kazakhstan v. Duman Mukhammedkarim
outcome_summary: Duman Mukhammedkarim's seven-year prison sentence was upheld by an Almaty regional court in November 2024.
notes: Appeal rejected; later reversal or release unconfirmed.

outcome_summary: The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Marat Zhylanbaev's detention arbitrary in 2025 and called for his immediate release.
notes: UN finding; it does not confirm an actual release.

outcome_summary: Katanyu Pan Muenkhamruang was convicted on 22 November 2023 and sentenced to two years in prison, with bail pending appeal.
notes: June 2025 report says appeal pending; bail is not acquittal.

case: Fairness Report: Kazakhstan v. Nazym Tabyldieva
outcome_summary: Nazym Tabyldieva was convicted on 10 November 2023 and sentenced to 18 months of house arrest and a five-year social-media activity ban.
notes: Earlier investigation closure did not prevent the later conviction.

outcome_summary: Thach Setha was convicted in both monitored cases in 2023 and received 18 months for forgery and three years for incitement.
notes: Earlier pardon and separate acquittal do not resolve these convictions.

outcome_summary: All seven Abzas Media defendants were convicted in June 2025 and sentenced to 7.5 to nine years; the Supreme Court rejected the final cassation appeals in April 2026.
notes: July 2026 report confirms the Supreme Court upheld the convictions.
